headline: No money-making rule has been proven yet. The paper bot runs, but its strategies earn about zero on honest 2016-24 data.
holdout: 2025+ data is sealed and untouched (0 of 1 uses).

findings.text: The bot's six replayable strategies earn about zero on honest 2016-24 data (2022-24 Sharpe +0.01).

Its losses are concentrated: 69 of 1,325 replayed trades (5%) lost more than 25% each. Together they lost $46,369, while all trades together made $5,574. The worst were speculative names such as SKYH, RIOT, AMC, ANVS (de-SPACs, meme, crypto and small biotech stocks). The bot's stops on its momentum strategies sit 26-29% below entry (median), and 11 were at or below zero. Screening out volatile stocks did not fix it (Area F).
QuantLab's real, tested skill is forecasting how much a stock will move, not which way. Option prices already know most of it.
After big news jumps the average stock lags the market, and prices finish reacting to a headline within about 15 minutes. Chasing news is not an edge for this bot.

ideas.name: The bot's six replayable strategies, as configured

ideas.meaning: 46% of the bot's trades are in the most volatile fifth of stocks (momentum_trend 90%). Those trades averaged -0.8% against +0.4% for the rest, but removing them changed the book's Sharpe the wrong way in 2016-19 and 2022-24. Nothing changes in the bot.

ideas.meaning: It earns less in normal years but cut the 2000-12 fall from -55% to -22%. Insurance against a long bear market that costs about 2.6 points a year when markets rise.

ideas.name: Both rules together
ideas.question: Does a simple rule beat holding the whole US market (1963-2024)?
ideas.meaning: Lower returns than simply holding the market, with no better risk-adjusted return out of sample.

ideas.meaning: Trading in and out every day costs more than the overnight effect is worth.

fixes.title: Fake price crashes from spin-offs and share distributions
fixes.detail: Alpaca's adjusted prices showed fake falls such as NVS -82% (Alcon spin-off, real move -12%) and UHAL -90% (holders were actually up about 8%). 94 bad stock-days flagged and repaired; 2 tickers reused by a different company cut off.

fixes.title: Every delisting booked as a -30% loss
fixes.detail: All 13 delisted trades in the bot's replay were cash takeovers at or above the last price, yet the rule booked each as -30%. This flips the bot's backtest from about zero to clearly negative and skews its own outcome statistics. Fix: takeovers with an Alpaca merger record exit at the last close, others keep -30%. Alpaca has records for 9 of those 13 (all 2022-24; almost none before 2020), so it fixes most takeovers from now on. 985 tests pass.

fixes.title: Spin-off days booked as real losses in the bot's live data
fixes.detail: The bot builds returns from raw prices, so a spin-off day looks like a crash. That can trigger a stop or a false 'buy the dip' signal. Fix: use the spin-off records the data vendor does provide.

fixes.title: Options matched to the wrong company
fixes.detail: Old option chains were joined to whichever company holds the ticker today (e.g. old Caesars vs Eldorado). One options result showed +31%; corrected, it is +4%.

fixes.title: Companies that later delisted silently dropped
fixes.detail: 14% of earnings events and 8% of option rows were missing, all from companies that later disappeared.

fixes.title: Overstated statistics
fixes.detail: Overlapping returns had inflated t-statistics about 1.7x; a placebo test compared earnings with earnings.

fixes.title: Replay dividend bias and a winner-picking bug
fixes.detail: Caught before any result was read: one-sided dividend rounding biased returns up; the leaderboard picked a 'winner' even when every option lost money.
